steps.question: Which genes change between the treated and the control sample within subject, across the 5 paired subjects, at BH-adjusted p < 0.05?

Redundant significant sets are collapsed and one representative per group is reported, with the full table retained as a supplement
Leading-edge genes with their Wald statistics are listed per significant set, and overlaps between the leading edges of reported sets are marked

steps.name: Reproducible report

steps.context: Consolidates T1S2 (primary DESeq2 result), T1S3 (limma-voom overlap and per-subject consistency) and T2S1 (preranked GSEA) into one document for a reader who did not run the analysis.
steps.question: What is the complete, reproducible account of the paired treated-versus-control analysis: design, thresholds, gene-level results, cross-method agreement, per-subject consistency and pathway signal?

constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the unshrunken estimate and its standard error in the table beside it
Report the number of significant genes from each method and the size of the intersection; do not present the union as the result

steps.description: Assemble the final report. State the method, the package versions, the design formula (~ subject + condition), the contrast and its direction (positive log2FoldChange = higher in treated), the thresholds (padj < 0.05, BH, independent filtering on), the number of genes tested after filtering and the number called per method. plan.title: Paired treated-vs-control DE in blood (5 subjects)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single raw integer count matrix (/eval-full-32-with-paired-n5-2/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 10 sample columns plus a gene-symbol first column) from STAR/featureCounts, with a 10-row sample table (/eval-full-32-with-paired-n5-2/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv: sample, subject, condition). Five human subjects each contribute one control and one treated blood sample, so the design is a complete, balanced paired design with n=5 pairs. The research question — which genes respond to treatment within each subject — is exactly the within-subject condition effect, so the subject must enter the model as a blocking term (~ subject + condition) rather than be ignored; a between-group test on these 10 samples would carry the between-subject variation into the residual and lose most of the power the pairing buys.

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC before any test: library sizes per sample, blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes coloured by condition and by subject, and a sample-distance heatmap. With paired blood samples the expectation is that samples cluster by subject rather than by condition — that is the signature of a design where blocking matters, and it is worth stating explicitly before the model. T1S1 also verifies the metadata really is 5 complete pairs (each subject exactly one control and one treated), because the blocked design is only estimable if it is.

T1S2 fits the DESeq2 model on the raw counts: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in at least 5 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, design ~ subject + condition with the reference level of condition set explicitly to the untreated/control level so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated, Wald test on the condition coefficient, apeglm shrinkage of that coefficient for ranking and plotting, BH adjustment with independent filtering at alpha 0.05. Four residual degrees of freedom is thin: the p-value histogram is inspected before the adjustment is trusted, and DESeq2's Cook's-distance outlier flagging (which sets p to NA rather than replacing counts below 7 replicates per cell) is left on with the flagged count reported separately from the independently filtered NAs.

T1S3 is the robustness cross-check the paired design permits: limma-voom on the same counts with the same blocked design (the knowledge service names limma-voom, not edgeR QL, as the alternative for a blocking factor here). It reports the overlap with the DESeq2 call set and treats the intersection as high-confidence, the method-specific calls as secondary. It also gives the per-subject view the question literally asks for: a paired log2 ratio (treated/control) per subject per gene for the top genes, so a reader can see whether a called gene moves in all five subjects or is driven by one pair. That per-subject consistency count is the honest answer to "within each subject" — with n=5 there is no power to test each subject separately, and the plan says so rather than pretending otherwise.

T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes (ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — the disputed choice is stated: the Wald statistic scales the effect by its uncertainty, unlike an unshrunken fold change, and does not saturate into ties like a signed p-value) and runs fgsea against the human MSigDB Hallmark collection first, then a Reactome collection as the second pass if one is provisioned. Given 5 pairs, the gene-level list may well be short, in which case the ranked method is the only defensible enrichment and no over-representation test is run.

T1S4 assembles the report: design, contrast, thresholds, number of genes tested and called, MA and dispersion plots, p-value histogram, the gene table carrying unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, the DESeq2/limma-voom overlap, leading-edge genes per significant set, and a full reproducibility record.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes, subject pairing check
Blocked design ~ subject + condition with explicit reference level control
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test with paired design ~ subject + condition (robustness cross-check)
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome
Reproducible report: MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, gene table with shrunken and unshrunken LFC, DESeq2/edgeR overlap, leading edge genes, sessionInfo

steps.name: limma-voom cross-check and per-subject consistency
steps.question: Which of the DESeq2 calls are reproduced by limma-voom on the same paired design, and for each called gene, in how many of the 5 subjects does the treated-versus-control change go in the reported direction?
steps.description: Two parts. (1) Robustness: refit the same comparison with limma-voom on the same filtered counts, using TMM scaling factors and the same blocked design ~ subject + condition, with eBayes moderation and BH adjustment at 0.05. Report the number of significant genes from each method and the size of the intersection; treat the intersection as the high-confidence set and list method-specific calls as a secondary set naming the method that called them. Do not present the union as the result. (2) Per-subject view: for the union of called genes (or, if fewer than 20 genes are called, the top 50 by shrunken log2 fold change), compute the per-subject paired log2 ratio of treated over control from DESeq2-normalized counts (with a small pseudocount) and tabulate, per gene, how many of the 5 subjects move in the same direction as the pooled estimate. Draw a heatmap of these per-subject log2 ratios (genes x 5 subjects) and paired line/dot plots for the top genes with the 5 subject pairs connected. State plainly that with one pair per subject there is no within-subject replication, so per-subject direction counts are descriptive consistency, not per-subject significance tests.
steps.context: The research question asks which genes respond within each subject. The pooled blocked model answers the average within-subject effect; this step reports how consistent that effect is across the 5 individual pairs, and cross-checks the call set with a second method.
acceptance_criteria: limma-voom is fit on the same filtered count matrix with TMM scaling and the same ~ subject + condition design

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic
steps.question: Which hallmark and pathway gene sets are coordinately shifted by treatment across the 5 paired blood samples?
steps.description: Run fgsea on the full ranked list of all genes tested in T1S2 — not a thresholded list — ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the 'stat' column). The ranking metric is a stated choice: the Wald statistic is used because it scales the effect by its standard error, unlike an unshrunken fold change which is large and noisy for low-count genes, and it does not produce the tied ranks that a saturated signed p-value gives. Genes are identified by HGNC symbol in counts.csv; map symbols to the identifier space of the gene set collection using the human organism annotation package, report the share of tested genes that failed to map, and drop many-to-many mappings with a stated count. First pass: the human MSigDB hallmark gene set collection. Second pass: a human Reactome/curated-pathway collection if one is provisioned in the reference store; if no Reactome collection is available, use the human WikiPathways collection that is present and say in the output which collection was actually used and why. Restrict to sets with 15 to 500 members after intersecting with the tested genes. Set and record a random seed for the permutations. Collapse redundant significant sets (fgsea's collapsePathways) and report one representative per group, keeping the full table as a supplement. For each significant set, list the leading-edge genes with their gene-level Wald statistic, and mark leading-edge overlap between reported sets. If fewer than about 50 genes reached padj < 0.05 in T1S2, do not run any over-representation test — report only the ranked result and state the size of the significant gene list.
steps.context: Human blood, treated vs control within subject. The reference store contains an MSigDB human hallmark GMT and human WikiPathways GMT; a Reactome collection may or may not be provisioned. Enrichment here enriches interpretation — if a collection is missing the analysis loses an annotation layer, not its answer.

steps.name: Reproducible report
steps.question: What is the complete, reproducible account of the paired treated-versus-control analysis: design, thresholds, gene-level results, cross-method agreement, per-subject consistency and pathway signal?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. State the method, the package versions, the design formula (~ subject + condition), the contrast and its direction (positive log2FoldChange = higher in treated), the thresholds (padj < 0.05, BH, independent filtering on), the number of genes tested after filtering and the number called per method. Place the fit diagnostics before the gene tables: the MA plot (shrunken fold changes against mean normalized count, significant genes marked), the dispersion plot, and the p-value histogram with its shape described. The gene table carries, for every reported gene, the unshrunken log2FoldChange, the shrunken (apeglm) log2FoldChange, the lfcSE, the Wald stat, the p-value and padj — genes are ranked and plotted by the shrunken value, never by the unshrunken value alone. Include the DESeq2/limma-voom overlap with the intersection labelled the high-confidence set, and the per-subject consistency table and heatmap from T1S3. Include the enrichment section naming the gene set database and version, the ranking metric (Wald statistic), the universe (tested genes), the size window (15-500), the tool and version, the multiple testing method, and the leading-edge genes of each significant set; state that enrichment results are method-dependent and are hypotheses for follow-up. Close with a reproducibility record: sessionInfo, every package version, the random seed used for the permutations, the gene set collection versions, and the fact that gene identifiers are HGNC symbols as supplied in counts.csv with no genome build or annotation release recorded in the input (say so rather than inventing one). State the power limitation plainly: 5 pairs, 4 residual degrees of freedom, and any negative or short result should be read as underpowered rather than as evidence of no effect.
